messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Whenever a book's cover changes, `Book::CoverProcessingJob` (in `app/jobs`)
is kicked off from the `Book` model and stamps the cover's SHA-256
fingerprint into the blob's metadata. In production it fails intermittently:
the worker picks it up before the database transaction that attached the
cover has committed, finds no file, and raises
`ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError`. Worse, when a save inside a larger
transaction is rolled back, the work for the never-committed cover is still
handed off — and errors on every retry. The search entry a book edit
refreshes goes the same way, off the same handover.

Fix when that background work is handed off. It should not be handed off
until the edit that kicked it off has committed, never while that edit is
still open — and if the edit is abandoned, it must never be handed off at
all.

The nightly importer runs the same edit over a whole batch, and applies the
batch all or nothing, so this has to hold there too. One thing must survive an
abandoned batch, though: the operator still hears that their import did not go
through. Losing that is how a failed import goes unnoticed until somebody asks.

On a successful edit the outcome is unchanged: the work still runs, the same
fingerprint is stamped and the search entry is refreshed. No new tables or
columns, and `bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it.

require "test_helper"

# Temporary reproduction (lives outside the repo).
class CoverHandoffReproTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  Handoff = Struct.new(:job_class, :arguments, :edit_open, :cover_uploaded, keyword_init: true)

  # Records every handoff to the queue together with the state seen at that moment.
  class SpyAdapter < ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::TestAdapter
    class << self
      attr_accessor :handoffs
    end

    def enqueue(job)
      record(job)
    end

    def enqueue_at(job, _timestamp)
      record(job)
    end

    private
      def record(job)
        book = job.arguments.first
        blob = book.cover.blob if book.is_a?(Book) && book.cover.attached?
        SpyAdapter.handoffs << Handoff.new(
          job_class: job.class,
          arguments: job.arguments,
          # joinable == the app's edit transaction is still open
          edit_open: ActiveRecord::Base.connection.current_transaction.joinable?,
          cover_uploaded: blob ? blob.service.exist?(blob.key) : nil
        )
      end
  end

  setup do
    @previous_adapter = ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter
    ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = SpyAdapter.new
    SpyAdapter.handoffs = []
    @previous_cache = Rails.cache
    Rails.cache = ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore.new
  end

  teardown do
    ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = @previous_adapter
    Rails.cache = @previous_cache
  end

  def cover_upload
    { io: File.open(file_fixture("pixel.bmp")), filename: "pixel.bmp", content_type: "image/bmp" }
  end

  def handed_off(klass)
    SpyAdapter.handoffs.select { it.job_class == klass }
  end

  test "A: successful edit hands off cover job after commit, with file uploaded" do
    books(:handbook).apply_edit(title: "Renamed", cover: cover_upload)

    cover = handed_off(Book::CoverProcessingJob)
    search = handed_off(Book::SearchIndexJob)
    puts "\n[A] handoffs: " + SpyAdapter.handoffs.map { |h| [h.job_class.name, h.edit_open, h.cover_uploaded] }.inspect
    assert_equal 1, cover.size
    assert_equal 1, search.size
    assert_not cover.first.edit_open, "cover job handed off while edit still open"
    assert cover.first.cover_uploaded, "cover job handed off before file was uploaded"
    assert_not search.first.edit_open, "search job handed off while edit still open"
  end

  test "B: abandoned edit (rolled back) hands off no cover or search job" do
    Book.transaction do
      books(:handbook).apply_edit(title: "Abandoned", cover: cover_upload)
      raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
    end

    puts "\n[B] handoffs: " + SpyAdapter.handoffs.map { |h| [h.job_class.name, h.edit_open, h.cover_uploaded] }.inspect
    assert_empty handed_off(Book::CoverProcessingJob)

    assert_not_equal "Imported", books(:handbook).reload.title
    assert_not books(:handbook).cover.attached?
    assert_empty handed_off(Book::CoverProcessingJob)
    assert_empty handed_off(Book::SearchIndexJob)
    failures = handed_off(Books::ImportFailureJob)
    assert_equal 1, failures.size, "operator was not told the import failed"
    assert_equal users(:kevin).id, failures.first.arguments.first
  end

  test "D: successful importer batch hands off cover and search jobs after the batch commits" do

All four scenarios now fail the way the issue describes:

- **A:** the successful edit hands the cover job off while the transaction is open, before the file exists.
- **B:** the rolled-back edit still hands off the cover job.
- **C:** the failed importer batch hands off the cover and search jobs. The failure notice is also handed off inside the open transaction, which is the behaviour I need to keep.
- **D:** the successful batch hands off the work while the batch is still open.

The fix has three parts:

1. Have `CoverProcessingJob` and `SearchIndexJob` opt in to Rails' built-in `enqueue_after_transaction_commit`. That defers the handoff until the outermost transaction commits, and drops it if the transaction rolls back. The batch case is covered because the importer's outer transaction is the one that gets the deferral.
2. Pin `ImportFailureJob` to `enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false`. Otherwise a global config change to `load_defaults 8.2` would defer it, and it would be silently dropped on rollback.
3. Send the importer's failure notice after the batch's transaction block, so it's sent once the rollback has happened, and also covers errors raised while committing.

I'll make the job changes first.

The background work is now handed off only after the edit commits. It is dropped if the edit is rolled back, and the importer's failure notice still goes out when a batch is abandoned. `bin/rails test` is still green (179 runs, 0 failures), and RuboCop is clean on the changed files.

**What was wrong:** `Book::Editing#apply_edit` enqueued both jobs inside its transaction. The cover job could run before the commit, and the rollback didn't cancel the enqueue.

**What I changed (four files, no tests, schema or config touched):**

- `app/jobs/book/cover_processing_job.rb` and `app/jobs/book/search_index_job.rb`: set `self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true`. This uses ActiveJob's built-in deferral in Rails 8.2. The enqueue waits for the outermost transaction to commit, and it is discarded on rollback. The `set(wait: 5.seconds)` delay is preserved.
- `app/jobs/books/import_failure_job.rb`: pinned to `enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false`. That keeps the notice from being deferred and then dropped by a rollback, even if the app-wide default is ever changed.
- `app/controllers/books/imports_controller.rb`: the failure notice is now sent in the rescue around the whole `Book.transaction` call, so it fires after the rollback and also covers errors during commit.

Because the importer runs everything in one outer transaction, the batch's work is handed off only if the whole batch commits. The `apply_edit` code itself didn't change.

**Verification:** I wrote a reproduction outside the repo, with a spy queue adapter that records, at each handoff, whether the edit was still open and whether the cover file existed. Before the fix, the cover and search jobs were handed off during the open edit, and the cover file wasn't uploaded yet. After the fix:

- A successful edit, a successful batch, and a web update hand off after commit, with the file uploaded. Running the handed-off jobs gives the same SHA-256 and the same search entry.
- An abandoned edit, a rolled-back savepoint, and a failed batch hand off no cover or search work.
- A failed batch still hands off `ImportFailureJob` with the operator's id.

I also ran a check against a throwaway SQLite database with real outermost transactions and no test fixtures. It showed the same results.

**Limitations and things I noticed:**

- Work is now enqueued after commit, so if the queue is unreachable at that moment, the edit is saved but its background work is lost. Previously, a queue failure rolled back the edit. This is the usual trade-off of after-commit enqueueing.
- In a failed batch, if the commit itself fails after data is written, the operator could be told the import failed even though it committed. I judged that the safer direction to err in.
- Pre-existing and not changed: if an in-memory `Book` is reused after a rolled-back cover change, a later plain save of that object persists the abandoned cover. The original code does the same, and the importer loads each book fresh per request, so it isn't reachable there.
